alignment.label: Alignment
alignment.fileOffsetWarning: File-offset alignment: bytes at the same position may not be the same address.
alignment.truncatedTitle: The aligned window was clipped to the shortest dump; bytes past the clip are not compared.
alignment.discardSummary: Why are bytes missing? {{discarded}} bytes ({{percent}}%) were left out of this comparison
alignment.discardIntersection: The aligned window holds only memory that EVERY selected dump captured, at the same ASLR-invariant address. A page one dump never captured - or never mapped - is left out for all of them, so gaps are normal and are not a sign that anything went wrong.
alignment.discardAnonymousOrdinal: Anonymous mappings have no name to align by, so they are keyed by type, size and the order they appear in within each dump. One extra anonymous mapping in one dump shifts the order of every later one, which can drop whole stretches of memory from the comparison.
alignment.discardNotMismatch: Bytes left out are drawn as hatched cells in the grid, never as a difference: "this page was not captured" and "this byte changed" are different findings.

alignSwitch.label: Align
alignSwitch.deltaFitTitle: Put bytes in correspondence by ASLR-invariant address, so the same address in every dump lands in the same column.
alignSwitch.rawOffsetsTitle: Compare byte 0x1000 with byte 0x1000, ignoring where either was mapped. Expect a flood of variance — that is the control condition, not a finding.
alignSwitch.rawCaution: Raw offsets is the control condition. Nothing here is aligned, so almost every byte differs — that flood is expected, and it is evidence the delta-fit build is doing work, not a finding about memory.

regions.chipTitle: Show every {{label}} region in this dump
regions.title: Regions
regions.approximate: spans a page boundary — range is approximate
regions.empty: No region of this class is at least the minimum length. Try the Changing chip — a real key is class-mixed, so a single-class query can miss it entirely.
regions.jumpTitle: Jump the viewer to this region
regions.jumpUnavailable: No navigable offset for this region in the current view — see the note above.
regions.noJump: These regions cannot be jumped to in the current view: the consensus is in raw file offsets while the viewer is addressing virtual addresses, or the anchor dump is still locked. Unlock the anchor, or switch the viewer's coordinate.
regions.differsWindowOnly: Differs is computed from the bytes currently loaded, not from the whole dump — the count and the list describe the window in view.
regions.mixedClassNote: Real key material is class-mixed: a planted 48-byte TLS secret classifies as 27 key candidate + 18 pointer + 3 structural bytes, so a single-class query shatters it into shards shorter than the minimum length and can return nothing at all. Changing queries all three non-invariant bands at once and keeps it whole.

desc.invariant: — every compared dump holds the same value here. Constants, code, padding.
desc.structural: — the value moves a little between dumps: lengths, counters, flags, small indices.
desc.pointer: — the value moves the way an address does: heap and stack pointers shifted by allocation and ASLR.
desc.keyCandidate: — the value is different in every dump with no structure to it. That is what an ephemeral secret looks like, and it is also what a nonce, a random ID or an uninitialised buffer looks like.
desc.differs: — the aligned dumps simply do not agree on this byte. Drawn as a ring around the byte rather than a fill, so it composes with whichever class colour is underneath instead of hiding it.

varianceLegend.thresholdsUnknown: This build did not report the variance bands it used, so the boundaries above are omitted rather than guessed.
varianceLegend.invariantDimmed: Invariant is deliberately dimmed. It is almost every byte in a dump, and it is the background the changing bytes have to stand out against — not a finding in itself.
varianceLegend.differsRing: Differs is a ring, not a fill, precisely so a byte can be both "pointer" and "the dumps disagree here" at once.
varianceLegend.mixedClass: A region is rarely one class. A planted 48-byte TLS secret measured here as 27 key candidate + 18 pointer + 3 structural bytes, so asking for key candidates alone can return nothing. The Changing chip asks for all three non-invariant bands together.
